svg.text: C-A STACK — cans, sleeves and discs under a quill
One rim (R260) for every can, sleeve and disc. Food goes down through the stack; between cans it moves by turning a closed pair over.
rim R260: flange Ø290, bore Ø250
quill: 8 kN press, spin 0–6000 rpm, Z 300
turns about a horizontal axis, 0–30 rpm
nothing is poured through open air,
powder and splash stay inside the pair
chamber Ø360 × 380, cone floor to drain
every point passes every jet: no spray shadow
then the wet steel is heated to 105 °C for 60 s
≈ 20 Wh instead of 300 Wh of 80 °C rinse water
THE KIT, one rim R260 (to scale): no part has a bearing, seal or motor

g.text: 1/7 Halved potatoes drop into the feed tube; below it: dicing grid disc, then the receiving can on the turntable.
2/7 Quill pushes the comb piston at 10 mm/s; the can turns with a knife on its rim and cuts the sticks into dice.
3/7 The comb studs pass through the grid: the last plug falls into the can, the grid leaves almost clean.
4/7 Inverter: can and an empty pot clamped rim to rim, then turned over together (hourglass).
5/7 Dice now lie in the pot; the emptied can leaves upside down, already draining.
6/7 Wash lathe: the part turns past a fixed row of jets, so every point is sprayed.
7/7 Induction flash: the wet steel itself is heated to 105 °C, which sanitises and dries it.
